about: The shared definition of what 'my work' is and the order it is owed, for
Mac, iOS, and web. A task from Core and an issue from GitHub are two rows
in two systems, but one question -- 'what do I owe' -- and the bug this
table exists to prevent is each surface answering it with its own filter,
its own ordering, and a vendor seam the reader never asked about.
Swift: Sources/WorkItems.swift. TypeScript: packages/contracts/src/work-items.ts.
Version 2 adds `stages`: where a row sits in the pipeline, and how a
stage is written back. See docs/BOARD.md.
`events` adds the phase of an event subject: its one date against the reader's today. See docs/EVENTS.md.
`unowned` adds open work nobody on our side holds. See docs/BOARD.md §Unowned.
rules: OPEN: the plan holds open work only. A completed or cancelled task and a
closed issue are history, never planned.
DEDUPE: a live task that carries a githubRef claims that issue -- the task
is the one row, because it holds the date and the subject. The issue with
that id is dropped. A done task claims nothing: its still-open issue is
real work and keeps its row.
SECTIONS, in order: inbox, late, today, soon, undated. inbox = not filed
to any subject, whatever its date -- filing comes before scheduling.
late/today/soon compare the due date's civil day in `timeZone` against
now's, never raw timestamps: work due earlier today is due today, not
late. undated = no due date, or one nobody can parse; every issue lands
here, because GitHub issues carry no due date.
ORDER: late/today/soon by due ascending -- the oldest debt first. inbox
and undated by updatedAt descending -- recent movement first, silence
last. Every tie breaks on id ascending. `order` is the sections
concatenated in section order.
COUNTS: open = every planned row after dedupe; late = the late section.

itemFields.id: stable identity; for an issue, its owner/repo#number
itemFields.filed: belongs to a project or lead; every issue is filed by construction
itemFields.dueDate: ISO 8601 or null; issues carry none
itemFields.githubRef: owner/repo#number a promoted task points at, else null

about: One stage vocabulary for the board: where a piece of work sits in the
pipeline, whichever store holds it. A Core task says it with `status`; a
GitHub issue says it with `state`, `state_reason` and its `agent:*`
labels. The bug this table prevents is a task half of the board with
four columns and an issue half with six.
rules: TASK: pending = queued, in_progress = doing, review = review, blocked =
blocked, completed = done, cancelled = dropped. A status nobody knows is
queued: it is open work until Core says otherwise, which is the same
reading `done` gives it.
ISSUE CLOSED: state_reason not_planned or duplicate = dropped; anything
else, including no reason, = done.
ISSUE OPEN: the stage label decides. agent:failed = blocked, agent:review
= review, agent:building = doing; agent:queued or no stage label = queued.
When more than one stage label is on the issue the strongest claim on a
person's attention wins: blocked over review over doing. Labels compare
case-insensitively. Any other label, agent:* or not, is not a stage.
WRITE TASK: the stage's status, verbatim, even the two Core does not
accept yet (review, blocked): the write is refused loudly there, never
translated silently here.
WRITE ISSUE: every stage label (agent:queued, agent:building,
agent:review, agent:failed) comes off, other labels keep their order,
and the stage's own label goes on the end: doing = agent:building, review
= agent:review, blocked = agent:failed. queued adds none, because a card
queued for a person is not queued for an agent; the hand-off labels it.
done = closed + completed, dropped = closed + not_planned; every open
stage sends state open, so a move out of done reopens.
BOARD: a card's stage is its own, except a live task that carries a
githubRef, which claims its issue: the task's stage is the card's, and the
issue is dropped from the board. Live means stage not done and not
dropped. Open columns keep the order the plan gives (late, today, soon,
then undated by movement). done and dropped order by updatedAt descending,
silence last, ties on id. `finishedSince` drops a finished card whose
updatedAt is older; one with no updatedAt stays, because nobody can say
it is old.
RECENTLY FINISHED: merge the done and dropped cards by updatedAt
descending, silence last, ties on id ascending. The board's
finishedSince window applies before the list is returned. The recovery
list only offers completed/cancelled tasks and closed issues; declined
task proposals remain a deliberate answer, not an undo action.

HOLDER: an open issue with any stage label (agent:queued, agent:building, agent:review, agent:failed) is an agent's, as UNOWNED reads it; a closed issue, an issue with no stage label, and every task are a person's. The filter is anyone, people, agents, or agent:<email>, matched case-insensitively against the agent the card's project names.

TASK FILTERS (meet#1222): `passesTaskFilter(item, {due, side}, now, timeZone)`. Overdue is open work due before today in the zone's civil days. An issue shows only while both filters are `any`. A task with no side reads as `unassigned`.

about: An event (a CMS row) has one date and no status field: the date is the
status. The phase is computed against the reader's today, in the reader's
zone, and never stored.
rules: PHASE: eventDate is a plain YYYY-MM-DD. Its civil day against today's
civil day in `timeZone`: earlier = past, same = live, later = upcoming.
COUNTDOWN: daysUntil is the civil-day difference from today in `timeZone`.
A positive day count is shown as days left; zero is Today; null is Upcoming.
UNDATED: null or unparseable is upcoming. A draft with tasks is open work;
hiding it would hide the tasks. It has no sort key and lists last.
OPEN: upcoming and live are open subjects; past is closed.

phaseCases.name: the reader's zone decides today: still the 19th in Los Angeles
the reader's zone decides today: already the 20th in Tokyo

about: Open work nobody on our side holds, across every subject: the
accountability list on Work's Overview. The Worker applies it to the
board's read and answers GET /api/crm/unowned; clients plan the rows
they get the way they plan Mine. See docs/BOARD.md §Unowned.
rules: OPEN: the board's open -- stage not done and not dropped. A proposed task
is a question for INBOX, never a card, so it is never unowned.
DEDUPE FIRST: the plan runs before the rule, so a live promoted task is
judged and the issue it claims is dropped whoever holds it.
TASK: unowned when it has no assignee and the client does not owe it.
responsibleParty team and unassigned are both ours; client is theirs. A
blank assignee is no assignee.
ISSUE: unowned when it has no assignee and no stage label. Any of
agent:queued, agent:building, agent:review, agent:failed means an agent
holds it; labels compare case-insensitively. Other labels say nothing.
ORDER: the plan's -- late, today, soon by due ascending, then undated by
updatedAt descending; ties on id.

cardFields.assignee: task only: the Core person it is assigned to, or null
cardFields.responsibleParty: task only: team, client or unassigned

cases.name: a promoted task is judged, never the issue it claims

about: The slice of Mine for Mine's Focus filter, the menu bar, the widget and the watch (planFocus).
Items are cards: the plan's item fields plus the stage fields under stages.cardFields.
rules: DATES: late and today come from dateSection with filing left out, so an unfiled late task is late on Home.
ORDER: late, then today, each by due date (ties on id); then started work, by recent movement.
STARTED: an open row not late or today whose stage is doing, review or blocked, whatever its date.
NEXT: when late, today and started are all empty, the first 3 soon rows by due date, and next is true.
FILTER: Mine's focus filter keeps the focus rows in the plan's own order, and never the Next fill.
COUNTS: lateCount and todayCount count the late and today rows; both are 0 under Next.

a clear day fills with the next three soon rows
